name: PM Fasal Bima Yojana (Crop Insurance)
summary: India's flagship crop insurance scheme, protecting farmers against yield loss from natural calamities, pests, and diseases at a heavily subsidised premium.
eligibility: All farmers growing notified crops in notified areas, with an insurable interest in the crop
Loanee farmers (those with Seasonal Agricultural Operations loans) are covered automatically
Non-loanee farmers can opt in voluntarily
Valid land ownership record or land tenure/lease agreement required
documents: Land ownership record or tenancy/lease agreement
Sowing certificate/declaration of crop and area
fee: Farmer pays only 2% of the sum insured for Kharif crops, 1.5% for Rabi crops, and 5% for horticultural/commercial crops; the rest of the actuarial premium is subsidised by the central and state governments.
process: Loanee farmers are enrolled automatically by their lending bank unless they opt out
Non-loanee farmers apply via the PMFBY portal, a participating bank, or a Common Service Centre before the season's cut-off date
Declare the crop, area, and land details, and pay the farmer's share of the premium
In case of crop loss, report it within the notified window via the app/portal or through the local agriculture office
Claim is assessed via Crop Cutting Experiments/remote sensing and settled to the farmer's bank account

faq.question: Is PMFBY compulsory for all farmers?
faq.answer: It's compulsory for farmers who have taken a Seasonal Agricultural Operations (crop) loan from a bank, unless they actively opt out. It's entirely voluntary for non-loanee farmers.

faq.question: How much premium does a farmer actually pay?
faq.answer: Just 2% of the sum insured for Kharif crops, 1.5% for Rabi crops, and 5% for horticultural/commercial crops — the government subsidises the rest of the actuarial premium.
